rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At every thing’s origin and each moment of its development, signs of God’s lordship and proofs of power and unity are evident to scholars, the learned, and all who can believe.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı her şeyin gerek mebde’inde ve gerek seyr-i tekâmülünün her lahzasında hem ehl-i ilme hem ehl-i fıkh u hikmete

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad name jinn can cover concealed beings and invisible metaphysical powers or spiritual substances to which people assign divinity, lordship, creative agency, or inherent influence as partners with or beneath God.
rows.anchor: “Cin” nâm-ı umûmîsi altında dâhil olan, nazarlardan mestur karanlık mahlûkāta

rows.speaker: Müfessirîn
rows.claim: Commentators take jinn here in a broader sense that includes angels and devils.
rows.anchor: Müfessirînin beyânına göre buradaki cin, melâike ve şeytanlara dahi şâmil bir ma‘nâ-yı e‘amma masruftur.

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas derives jinn from concealment: angels and spirits are unseen, so they too may be called jinn; this also explains counting Iblis among the jinn.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas demiştir ki: “Cin lafzı istitardan müştaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discussing shirk in visible, physical things such as idols and stars, the passage turns to its philosophical source: treating angels, devils, intellect, soul, matter, forces, or nature as first or intermediate lords.
rows.anchor: Yukarıda asnâm ve nücûm gibi mahsüs ve fizikî şeylerden şerîk ittihaz edenlerin ashâb-ı asnâm

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some commentators say the verse was revealed about those who called the angels God’s daughters, and that angels are termed jinn here.
rows.anchor: Bazı müfessirînin beyânına göre bu âyet “melâike Allah’ın kızlarıdır” diyenler dolayısıyla nâzil olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling angels God’s daughters presupposes procreation and shared essence, a notion connected with the Sabians’ worship of angels.
rows.anchor: Melâikeye Allah’ın kızları demek de müşâreket-i cevheriye iktizâ eden tevlîd

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas links the verse to dualists who imagined kinship between God and Iblis like two brothers and held that God created good while Iblis created evil.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan bir rivayete göre de işbu وَجَعَلُوا۟ لِلَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ Sûre-i Sâffât’taki

rows.speaker: Mecus
rows.claim: Magi dualism divides all good between Light, or Yezdan, and all evil between Darkness, or Ahriman; the source calls this a general form of dualism.
rows.anchor: ale’l-umûm Mecus bu âlemdeki bütün hayırlar nûrdan ve ta‘bîr-i âharla Yezdan’dan, bütün şerler de zulmetten

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zindiq derives from the Persian association with Zoroaster’s Zend scripture; zenadiqa originally designated Magi generally.
rows.anchor: Zerdüşt’ün Zend kitâbına nisbeti ifade eden Fârisî’de “zendik”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because some Magian groups allowed marriage to close relatives, rejected halal and haram, or advocated sharing women and property, zindiq also came to mean irreligious or unbelieving by custom.
rows.anchor: “zındık” bilhassa dinsiz ve itikadsız mânasına da örf olmuş ise de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The material dualism expressed as Light and Darkness was condemned at the sūra’s opening; the metaphysical Yezdan–Ahriman partnership is also rejected here through the word jinn.
rows.anchor: Mecusun hissî bir nokta-i nazar iş‘âr eden nûr ve zulmet isimleriyle ifade ettikleri bu ikilik akideleri sûrenin başında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahriman is Iblis in Islamic terms, and Iblis is from the jinn according to the cited verse in al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: Çünkü Ehrimen İslâm’da İblis denilendir. Ve İblis مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ فَفَسَقَ

rows.speaker: Maniviyye ve Mezdekiyye
rows.claim: The Manicheans and Mazdakites are described as genuine dualists who make the good and evil principles equally eternal.
rows.anchor: tam mânasıyla seneviyye bulunan Maniviyye ve Mezdekiyye gibi mezhebler bulunduğu gibi

rows.speaker: Deysâniyye
rows.claim: The Deysaniyya and Marcionite groups add a third, mediating principle alongside the two opposing origins, yielding a triadic doctrine.
rows.anchor: bir asl-ı sâlis daha ilâve ederek teslîse kāil olan Deysâniyye

rows.speaker: Kiyûmresiyye, Zervâniyye, Zerdüştiyye, Meshiyye
rows.claim: Most old Magian schools did not place the evil principle on an equal level with the good one; they considered Ahriman originated rather than eternal.
rows.anchor: ekser Mecus ve ale’l-husûs Kiyûmresiyye, Zervâniyye, Zerdüştiyye, Meshiyye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite their differences, all Magian schools share the claim that Ahriman participates with God in governing this world, assigning good to God and evil to Iblis; in this broad sense they are dualists.
rows.anchor: hepsi bu âlem-i tedbirde Allah’a Ehrimen’i teşrik etmekte

rows.speaker: Şehristânî
rows.claim: Shahrastani says Magi divide good and evil, benefit and harm, and right and wrong between two origins, named Light and Darkness or Yezdan and Ahriman.
rows.anchor: Şehristânî der ki: “‘Ale’l- ‘umûm Mecus hayr u şerri, nef‘u darrı, salâh ve fesâdı beynlerinde tamamen inkısam etmiş

rows.speaker: Şehristânî
rows.claim: Shahrastani reduces Magian debates to two issues: how Light became mixed with Darkness and how Light will be freed from Darkness; they treat these as origin and final destiny.
rows.anchor: Mecus mesâilinin hepsi iki kāide üzerinde toplanır. Birincisi nûrun zulmet ile sebeb-i imtizâcı, ikincisi de nûrun zulmetten halâsı meseleleridir.

rows.speaker: Asıl Mecusîler
rows.claim: The original Magi hold that Light is eternal and Darkness originated, then dispute how Darkness arose: if Light did not create evil, who did, and how could the two principles mix?
rows.anchor: Bununla beraber asıl Mecusîler bu iki aslın ikisinin de kadîm-i ezelî olması câiz olamayacağına; Nûr’un ezelî, Zulmet’in muhdes olduğuna kāildirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author presents the Magian account as incoherent: if Light did not originate Darkness, no origin for evil or explanation for its mixture with Light remains.
rows.anchor: Bunu o ihdas etmemiş ise kim ihdas edebilir? İhdas edilmiş değil ise terkib ve imtizac nasıl mümkin olur?

rows.speaker: Kiyumresîler
rows.claim: Kiyumrasis say Light produced Darkness after wondering how it could have an opponent; Ahriman then rebelled, fought Light’s forces, was mediated with by angels, and was allotted the lower world for seven thousand years before yielding it back.
rows.anchor: Kiyumresîlere göre “Nûr, benim bir münâza‘acım olsa nasıl olur?” diye bir fikr etmiş

rows.speaker: Zervânîler
rows.claim: One Zervani account says Light created luminous spiritual beings first, but the chief figure Zervan’s doubt brought Ahriman, or Satan, into existence.
rows.anchor: Zervânîlere göre de Nûr evvelâ hepsi nûrdan birtakım eşhâs-ı rûhâniyye-i nûrâniye ibdâ‘etmiş

rows.speaker: Bazı Zervânîler
rows.claim: Another Zervani account says Zervan’s failed 9,999-year invocation and doubt produced twins: Ahriman from doubt and Hurmuz from knowledge; Ahriman emerged first by tearing the womb and seized the world.
rows.anchor: Bazı Zervânîler de demişler ki Zervân-ı kebîr, bir oğlu için 9999 sene zemzeme etmiş olmamış

rows.speaker: Zerdüşt
rows.claim: Zoroaster teaches two opposing principles whose mixture produces the world’s forms, while also saying that both principles and their mixture were created by the one God, who has no partner or equal.
rows.anchor: Zerdüşt de bu iki aslın mütezâd olup mevcûdât-ı âlemin iki mebde’i olduğunu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds a contradiction in attributing Ahriman’s creation and the mixture of the principles to God while insisting that Ahriman’s existence cannot be attributed to God.
rows.anchor: asl-ı şer olan Ehrimen’in zıddıyla beraber halkını ve bunların mezcini vâhid olan Allah teâlâ’ya nisbet ettiği hâlde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that Zoroaster’s scheme posits three governing lords beneath the first Creator: a good creator and an evil creator, themselves created principles of Light and Darkness.
rows.anchor: bir de vâhid olan Hâlık-ı evvel’in mâdûnunda biri hâlık-ı hayr

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zoroaster’s account, the author concludes, extends dualism from God versus Iblis to good from an angel and evil from Iblis, with their partnership ultimately attributed to God.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh Zerdüşt yalnız hayr Allah’tan ve şer İblis’ten demek tarzında sineviyyet ile kalmamış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse fits both reported occasions and, from its context, extends across forms of metaphysical and spiritual shirk, including dualism, tritheism, and related doctrines.
rows.anchor: Ve bu mâna ile âyet nakledilen sebeb-i nüzûlün ikisine de muntabık olduktan başka siyâk u sibaktan anlaşıldığına göre gerek sineviyye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural shurakāʾ rather than singular sharīk expresses the verse’s distributive breadth across many kinds of partners and shirk.
rows.anchor: şümûlü tevzî‘an anlatmak içindir ki شَرِيكًا değil شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn may include hidden natural forces treated as agents, as well as concealed beings, bodies, persons, or secret societies that can in principle be seen but remain out of sight.
rows.anchor: cinnin mefhûm-ı e‘ammında yalnız gayr-i mer’î olan ve ancak temessül hâlinde görülebilen kuvâ ve rûhâniyyet-i mücerrede değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the jinn; treating creatures as rivals to their Creator or imagining that they affect the world and people without divine permission wrongly implies divine incapacity.
rows.anchor: hâlbuki onları Allah halk etti. Yani cinler de Allah’ın mahlûkudur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in wa-khalaqahum may refer back to jinn, and this reading signals that jinn belong among rational beings.
rows.anchor: Bu mânaya göre وَخَلَقَهُمْ zamîri “cin”e râci‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun may refer to the polytheists who made partners, meaning God created those people, not the jinn; attributing independent influence to jinn is then grave ingratitude.
rows.anchor: Bu zamîrin “cin”e değil جَعَلُوا’nun fâili olan müşriklere ircâ‘ı da muhtemeldir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some invented divine sons and daughters by imagining procreation in God, then treated the alleged offspring as divine beings and worshipped them, often representing God and them with idols.
rows.anchor: birtakımları da Allah’a oğullar, kızlar uydurdular.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples include Arab polytheists and Sabians who called angels God’s daughters, some Magi who called Hurmuz and Ahriman sons, Jews who called Uzayr God’s son, and Christians who called the Messiah God’s son.
rows.anchor: bazı Mecus, “Üzeyr ibnullah” diyen bazı Yehûd

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Philosophers who teach emanation and generation resemble these groups; such claims lack knowledge and make their proponents ignorant fabricators who do not understand what they assert.
rows.anchor: Tekvinde sudur ve tevlîde kāil olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone positing two or three gods, or a lesser, equal, similar, or opposing partner in God’s essence, attributes, or acts, asserts a partner and shared kind; divine offspring claims entail the same error.
rows.anchor: İlâh ikidir veya üçtür diye Allah’a zâtında veya sıfâtında veya ef‘âlinde az veya çok muâdil veya mâdûn

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In his rendering, bi’t-temsîl makes the comparison explicit and yaldızlı (“gilded”) renders the disbelievers’ deeds as coated or prettified.
rows.anchor: hiç o bi’t-temsîl zulmetler içinde kalmış ve ondan bir türlü çıkamayacak bir hâlde bulunan kimse gibi olur mu?

words: كَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording recalls 6:108, where God says that each community’s deeds were made fair to it; the beautification here follows the same pattern.
rows.anchor: Yani bâlâda كَذَٰلِكَ زَيَّنَّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمْ [el-En‘âm 6/108] buyurulmamış mı idi?

words: كَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beautification comes from devils through their misleading promptings and from God in the sense that He creates those promptings as they occur.
rows.anchor: Şeytanların yaldızlı ilkāâtı itibariyle şeytanlar tarafından ve o ilkāât esnasında halk tarîkiyle de Allah tarafındandır.

words: كَذَٰلِكَ زُيِّنَ لِلْكَٰفِرِينَ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because their deeds are beautified, disbelievers approve of what they do and cannot leave the darkness.
rows.anchor: Ve bu tezyin yüzündendir ki kâfirler yaptıklarını beğenir ve zulumâttan çıkamazlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about beautified deeds and remaining in darkness is not confined to the Meccans.
rows.anchor: Hem bu yalnız Mekkelilere mahsus da değildir:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A future day will bring all humans and jinn together for judgment.
rows.anchor: Düşün ki bir gün gelecek Allah o ins ü cinnin hepsini bir yere toplayacak;

words: يَٰمَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ قَدِ ٱسْتَكْثَرْتُم مِّنَ ٱلْإِنسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to the jinn assembly is glossed as addressing hidden devil societies that targeted and misled many humans, swelling their own company by drawing people into the devils’ ranks.
rows.anchor: ey ma‘şer-i cin, ey cin cemaati, ey gizli şeytan cemiyetleri; insten çoğuna göz diktiniz, çok iğvâ ve idlâl ettiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human allies are rendered as the jinn’s yardakları, their henchmen or followers.
rows.anchor: bunların insten olan yardakları

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn taught people routes to lust, deception, fraud, false reports, magic, and ways to spread corruption and hide; people gained pleasures, while jinn gained their aims through people’s willing acceptance and assistance.
rows.anchor: Cinler inse şehevât yollarını ve vesâitini gösterdiler, mekr ü hud‘a, tezvir ve erâcif, sihr ü efsun usullerini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humans’ willing acceptance and help mean responsibility belongs not only to their jinn companions; both sides benefited and share culpability.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh bu babda mes’ûliyet yalnız cin dostlarımızın değildir. Doğrusu biz yekdiğerimizden istifade ettik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human allies admit reaching the end of the respite God appointed for them, confessing their sins and their shared responsibility with the jinn.
rows.anchor: ve bizim için tâyin ve tesmiye ettiğin ecelimize yettik; bize verdiği mühletin nihâyetine erdik.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies the appointed term with the specified term mentioned at the sūra’s beginning and says that the appointed endpoint, the Day of Resurrection, has arrived.
rows.anchor: sûrenin başında وَأَجَلٌۭ مُّسَمًّى عِندَهُۥ ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ [6/2] diye beyan olunan ecel-i müsemmâ

words: ٱلنَّارُ مَثْوَىٰكُمْ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the exception says “what God wills” rather than “whom God wills,” he takes it to refer to periods of time, not particular people, within the promise of eternal residence in Hell.
rows.anchor: hulûd-ı nârdan bu istisnâ bazı eşhâsa değil, bazı ezmâna aittir.

words: ٱلنَّارُ مَثْوَىٰكُمْ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَآ إِلَّا مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says that in certain periods unbelievers will be taken from the fire, cast into the cold of zamharir, and then returned to the fire.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın dilediği bazı zamanlar küffâr ateşten çıkarılıp soğuğa, zemherîre atılacak, sonra yine nâra iade olunacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God perfectly orders His acts and knows the hidden and manifest states of all humans and jinn and the punishments they deserve; He judges with knowledge and will.
rows.anchor: ins ü cin bütün sekaleynin de gizli açık bütün hâllerini ve lâyık oldukları cezâları bilir.

words: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُوَلِّى بَعْضَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بَعْضًۢا بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes wrongdoers allies because their habitual acquisitions and conduct resemble one another; even without meeting, they become friends and defend each other.
rows.anchor: Kesbleri, âdetleri birbirlerine benzeyenler birbirlerini görmeseler bile uzaktan uzağa birbirlerine dost olurlar

words: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُوَلِّى بَعْضَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ بَعْضًۢا بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَكْسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the resurrection day, human and jinn wrongdoers will try to excuse one another because they shared wrongdoing, but their fellowship leads them to confess shared guilt, responsibility, and punishment.
rows.anchor: İns ü cinden zâlimler, haksızlar da kesbde müşareket ve mücânesetlerinden dolayı yekdiğerini mâzur göstermek isterken

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the jinn give no answer to the rebuke for misleading humans, their human allies step forward to excuse them, then confess mutual benefit and shared guilt.
rows.anchor: cin hiçbir cevap vermediği hâlde onların insten olan dostları, dostlukları muktezâsınca ortaya atılarak mes’ûliyeti üzerlerine alarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The confession shows humans and jinn to be one collective community with the same conscience, deeds, responsibility, and entitlement to the same punishment, rather than separate assemblies.
rows.anchor: cinnin ayrı, insin ayrı bir ma‘şer değil, hey’et-i mecmû‘asının bir ma‘şer; aynı vicdan, aynı kesb, aynı mes’ûliyet taşıyan
